notes:
SUMMARY: 50 images, all public domain / CC0 / CC BY / CC BY-SA (no NC/ND). Per era: origins 7, medieval 6, searoutes 4, plantation 8, bengal 8, synthetic 7, denim 4, revival 6. Licenses: Public domain 17, CC0 16, CC BY-SA 4.0 9, CC BY-SA 3.0 4, CC BY-SA 2.0 2, CC BY 2.0 1, CC BY 3.0 1. Sources: Met Open Access API (10), Cleveland Museum of Art Open Access API (5), Wellcome Collection catalogue API (6), Wikimedia Commons file pages (29; incl. NARA, British Library, Science History Institute, Tropenmuseum, ASC Leiden, Geograph uploads). Every item has verified=true: the rights statement quoted in rightsEvidence was read from the museum API response or from the Licensing/Permission section of the Commons file page (fetched with curl, not the rate-limited API).

IMAGE-URL CHECKS: Met, Cleveland and Wellcome thumb+full URLs all returned HTTP 200 image/* (curl -sI). Wikimedia: 28 of 29 thumbnails returned 200 image/* (thumbCheck field; the exception is the Tropenmuseum Yoruba photo, whose 700 px original doubles as its thumb); upload.wikimedia.org rate-limited (HTTP 429, 'robot policy') that one and most original-file requests, so those URLs are copied from each file page's 'Original file' link and the MD5 hash path was re-computed locally. Thumbnails of .tif/.pdf/.svg files use Commons' derived-JPEG/PNG patterns (lossy-page1-960px-…tif.jpg, page5-960px-…pdf.jpg, 960px-…svg.png). NOTE: Met 'web-large' thumbnails are only ~600 px on their long side (below the 800–1000 px target; the Met publishes no intermediate size) — use fullUrl (originals, 1–5 MB) and resize if larger thumbs are needed. Cleveland thumbs are its 'web' JPEGs (~900 px); fullUrl is the 'print' JPEG (up to 3400 px) rather than the multi-hundred-MB TIFF.

ERA ASSIGNMENTS THAT FOLLOW THE STORY RATHER THAN THE CAMERA DATE: modern photos of source plants (Indigofera tinctoria, woad, Persicaria, Strobilanthes, I. suffruticosa) are placed in 'origins'; the 2022 photo of woad cocagnes is 'medieval' (Toulouse woad trade); the Unicorn Tapestries (1495–1505) are 'searoutes'; BASF's 1881 works painting and the 2008 structural formula are 'synthetic'; the 1873 Davis/Levi Strauss rivet patent is 'denim'. The adire eleko panel (George V era, 1910–36) is 'synthetic'. Many coordinates are representative rather than exact — see each item's locationNote.

CAVEATS: (1) Unicorn tapestry: the Met object page could not be fetched (HTTP 429); that its catalogue text mentions woad is inferred from the Met API full-text search for 'woad' returning this object (the rights status itself is verified via isPublicDomain). (2) Faden 1780 cartouche: the NARA upload on Commons carries a PD-USGov tag, which is technically inapt for a 1780 London publication, but the map is public domain by age anyway. (3) Gandhi 1917: the portrait is the frontispiece of a 1917 book, not a photograph taken in Champaran; coordinates mark Champaran as the story location. (4) CC BY-SA items require attribution and share-alike on adaptations; Commons dual-licensed items (Tuareg2.JPG CC BY-SA 3.0/GFDL; Indigo-guizhou.jpg GFDL/CC BY 3.0) are listed under their CC option. (5) Captions say 'blue-dyed'/'resist-dyed' where the holding institution does not name indigo (Met blue-resist bed hanging; Met Ahmadabad stamp-resist cotton; Bruges manuscript).

REJECTED / NOT USED AND WHY: Art Institute of Chicago — its IIIF image server (www.artic.edu/iiif/2) returned a Cloudflare challenge (HTTP 403) from this machine, so thumbnails could not be verified; strong PD candidates if checked from a browser: AIC 248700 Soninke robe (boubou lomasa, 'Handspun cotton, indigo dye'), 273353 Dyula prestige cloth ('indigo dyed cotton'), 193241 Jingoji Sutra ('indigo-dyed paper'). Library of Congress — item pages and most JSON endpoints were Cloudflare/429-blocked; the LOC search API showed Mouzon's 1775 'Accurate Map of North and South Carolina' (gm71002153, 74692510), but its cartouche has no indigo vignette, so it was replaced by the indigo cartouche on Faden's 1780 South Carolina map (NARA copy); Mouzon's 1773 St Stephen's Parish map (which does have an indigo-process vignette) was not found in a verifiable free copy. William Morris 'Strawberry Thief' (AIC 149052, CMA 1937.696) — museum records do not mention indigo. Cleveland sutras on indigo-dyed paper (1916.1060, 1970.64) — images are extreme panoramas (e.g., 1263×52 px). Cleveland 1951.400 resist-dyed Coptic hanging and Met 309769 Sierra Leone hanging — dye not identified as indigo. Met 312915 Maya whistle — little visible Maya blue (used 313335 instead). Met 641560 'Blue Jeans' lithograph — a theatre poster, not denim. Wellcome 'Two men preparing dye' Indian watercolour — dye unidentified. Commons 'Gandhiji and Sub-Inspector Qurban Ali in Champaran (1917)' — provenance only a 2018 embassy tweet and the dress shown suggests a later date. Commons NARA 'Industries of War – Manufacturing denim at the White Oak Cotton Mills' (1917–18, PD) — card-mounted stereo views with a tiny image area. Commons Kofar Mata photo with '©SOLA SLV' watermark; 'Pays Dogon (9).JPG' (caption mismatch); 'নীলদর্পণ Nil Darpan.jpg' (photo of a modern edition cover — cover-design rights unclear); 'Indigofera tinctoria1.jpg' and '17-Cutting-Indigo-into-Cakes.jpg' (≤750 px); 'Furusyo aizome.jpg' (PD but shows only a building exterior).

GAPS (no verified free image found or chosen): colonial Guatemalan/Salvadoran obraje de añil and present-day El Salvador añil; Bamileke ndop cloth (Cleveland has CC0 Bamileke/Bamum objects with indigo — prestige stool 2006.138, headdress 2024.70 — but not ndop cloth); Pomet's 1694 indigo engraving and the Encyclopédie 'Indigoterie' plate specifically (covered instead by Leclerc/Du Tertre 1683, Beauvais-Raseau 1770 and a Radel/Bénard vat plate); Iron Age/Celtic woad and the ~6,000-year-old Huaca Prieta indigo cotton; Japanese sukumo; bio-indigo (bacterial/enzymatic) and a photo of synthetic indigo powder; a mid-century denim mill.
